name: Kong Gateway
summary: A Lua/OpenResty API gateway that matches routes to upstream services, executes scoped plugins in the proxy lifecycle, and can separate configuration control planes from traffic-serving data planes.

features.name: Route-to-service upstream abstraction
features.description: Routes match request criteria and forward to Gateway Services, which represent upstream connectivity and can be shared by multiple routes.
benefits: Separates client-facing matching from backend connectivity
costs: Route priority, path handling, timeouts, and retries affect proxy semantics

features.name: Scoped plugin lifecycle execution
features.description: Plugins implement lifecycle handlers and configuration schemas and can attach to routes or services to transform or control proxied traffic.
benefits: Adds reusable authentication, transformation, and policy stages
costs: Plugin ordering, scope, shared state, and database requirements complicate behavior

features.name: Control-plane/data-plane topology
features.description: Hybrid deployments separate configuration management in control-plane nodes from traffic serving in data-plane nodes, while traditional and DB-less modes provide alternate state topologies.
benefits: Allows geographically distributed data planes and cached last-known configuration
costs: Control-plane availability, configuration propagation, and plugin storage capabilities differ by topology

mathematical_views.question: Which highest-priority route matches a request and identifies the service and route-scoped policies?
assumptions: Routes are predicates over protocol, host, path, method, headers, port, or SNI
The router selects the highest-priority matching route
The view abstracts NGINX/OpenResty request parsing

mathematical_views.question: How do route, service, and global plugins transform a request and response across proxy lifecycle phases?
assumptions: Plugins are handlers attached to scoped entities
Lifecycle phases are ordered execution stages
The view does not claim that plugins are commutative or isolated

mathematical_views.question: When does configuration authored at a control plane become usable by a data plane serving traffic?
assumptions: Control-plane configuration is propagated over the Kong clustering channel
A data plane can continue with last-known configuration in hybrid mode
The model does not infer convergence latency or availability guarantees

benefits: Reusable backend definitions with multiple client-facing routes
costs: Matching and proxy options create a broad route/service configuration space

benefits: Extensible request policy without changing core routing
costs: Lifecycle ordering and plugin persistence needs complicate deployment
Configuration propagation and topology-specific plugin limitations require operational discipline
